input.rationale: With only 3 merit measurements, I targeted the Cu-modified BiVO4 region (the best-known visible-light photoanode, able to absorb 2.72 eV photons) and included one Cu-V-rich probe as a contrast. Index 0 (Bi0.36 Cu0.18 V0.46, slightly V-rich relative to 1:1 Bi:V, low Cu) gave the highest photocurrent at 2.65e-5 A. That is about twice index 34 (near-stoichiometric Bi:V) and about ten times the Cu-V-rich index 2.

rejected.reason: Measured 1.26e-5 A. Close to 1:1 Bi:V but lower than the slightly V-rich index 0.
Measured 2.2e-6 A. The Cu-V-rich (CuV2O6-like) region performs poorly.
Cu-rich oxides are expected to be poor photoanodes, and the Cu-V probe supports this. Not measured because the budget was limited.

content.text:
I've submitted the episode. The best result was **index 0 (Bi 0.36, Cu 0.18, V 0.46)**, with a photocurrent of **2.65×10⁻⁵ A**. How close that is to the library's true best is unknown, because I only got to measure 3 of the 284 compositions.

There were 3 photocurrent measurements and 5 XRD scans available. I started in the BiVO₄-like region, since BiVO₄ is the best-known photoanode in this Bi–Cu–V system and absorbs 455 nm light. I also measured one Cu–V-rich composition for contrast:

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.36 / 0.18 / 0.46 | **2.65×10⁻⁵** |
| 34 | 0.40 / 0.17 / 0.43 | 1.26×10⁻⁵ |
| 2 | 0.07 / 0.35 / 0.58 | 2.2×10⁻⁶ |

- **Cu–V-rich compositions did poorly.** Index 2 was about 10× weaker than index 0.
- **A slight excess of V over Bi helped.** Index 0, with a little more V than Bi, gave about twice the photocurrent of index 34, which is near 1:1.

**Limitations:**
- I didn't use any of the 5 XRD scans, so the phases behind these results weren't checked.
- The Gaussian-process suggestion tool wasn't useful with only two data points; its uncertainties were larger than its predictions. I chose the third composition by chemical reasoning instead.
- Nearby compositions with even more V, such as index 29 or 14, weren't measured and could beat index 0.
